articles.title: Tipping Etiquette and Norms Are in Flux—Here's How You Can Avoid Feeling Flustered or Ripped Off
articles.topic: 美国小费文化的变迁：数字支付系统的普及催生“小费渐涨”与“小费通胀”，如今给小费更具强制性、与服务质量脱钩，正逐渐成为顾客的一种负担
articles.source: 2025 年考研英语（二）Text 1 · 原文与答案依据真题及解析 PDF

sentences.en: U.S. customers historically tipped people they assumed were earning most of their income via tips, such as restaurant servers earning less than the minimum wage.
sentences.cn: 美国顾客历来会给那些他们认为通过小费获取大部分收入的人小费，比如收入低于最低工资标准的餐馆服务员。

words.meaning: n. （餐馆）服务员（server 的复数）

sentences.en: In the early 2010s, a wide range of businesses started processing purchases with iPads and other digital payment systems.
sentences.cn: 在21世纪10年代初，众多企业开始使用iPad和其他数字支付系统处理付款。

words.meaning: v. 处理（process 的现在分词）

sentences.en: These systems often prompted customers to tip for services that were not previously tipped.
sentences.cn: 这些系统常常提醒顾客为之前无须付小费的服务支付小费。

words.meaning: v. 促使，提示（prompt 的过去式）

sentences.en: Today's tip requests are often not connected to the salary and service norms that used to determine when and how people tip.
sentences.cn: 如今索要小费往往与过去常常决定人们何时以及如何给小费的工资和服务标准无关。

words.meaning: n. 请求，索要（request 的复数）
n. 标准，规范（norm 的复数）

sentences.en: Customers in the past nearly always paid tips after receiving a service, such as at the conclusion of a restaurant meal, after getting a haircut or once a pizza was delivered.
sentences.cn: 过去的顾客几乎总是在接受一项服务后才支付小费，比如在餐馆用餐结束时、理发完毕后或比萨送达时。

words.meaning: v. 递送，送达（deliver 的过去分词）

sentences.en: That timing could reward high-quality service and give workers an incentive to provide it.
sentences.cn: 这样的时间安排可以奖励高质量服务，并激励工作者提供优质服务。

sentences.en: It's becoming more common for tips to be requested beforehand.
sentences.cn: 预先索要小费变得越来越普遍。

sentences.en: And new tipping technology may even automatically add tips.
sentences.cn: 而且新的支付小费的技术甚至可能自动添加小费。

sentences.en: The prevalence of digital payment devices has made it easier to ask customers for a tip.
sentences.cn: 数字支付设备的普及使得向顾客索要小费变得更加容易。

words.meaning: n. 设备，装置（device 的复数）

sentences.en: That helps explain why tip requests are creeping into new kinds of services.
sentences.cn: 这有助于解释为什么索要小费正逐渐出现在新型服务中。

words.meaning: v. 逐渐出现，蔓延（creep 的现在分词）

sentences.en: Customers now routinely see menus of suggested default options—often well above 20% of what they owe.
sentences.cn: 顾客现在经常会看到附带着建议小费金额的默认选项的菜单——这些金额往往远高于他们应付金额的20%。

sentences.en: The amounts have risen from 10% or less in the 1950s to 15% around the year 2000 to 20% or higher today.
sentences.cn: 这一数额从20世纪50年代的10%或者更低，增长到2000年前后的15%，再到如今的20%或者更高。

words.meaning: n. 数额，金额（amount 的复数）
v. 上涨，增加（rise 的过去分词）

sentences.en: This increase is sometimes called tipflation—the expectation of ever-higher tip amounts.
sentences.cn: 这种增长有时被称为“小费通胀”——期望小费金额不断增长。

sentences.en: Tipping has always been a vital source of income for workers in historically tipped services, like restaurants, where the tipped minimum wage can be as low as US$2.13 an hour.
sentences.cn: 对于历来就收取小费的服务性行业（比如餐馆）的工作者来说，小费一直是重要的收入来源，在这些行业中，有小费的（员工的）最低工资可能低至每小时2.13美元。

sentences.en: Tip creep and tipflation are now further supplementing the income of many low-wage service workers.
sentences.cn: 小费渐涨和小费通胀如今正在进一步补充许多低薪服务行业工作者的收入。

words.meaning: v. 补充，增补（supplement 的现在分词）

sentences.en: Notably, tipping primarily benefits some of these workers, such as waiters, but not others, such as cooks and dishwashers.
sentences.cn: 值得注意的是，小费主要惠及这些工作者中的一部分，比如服务员，而不是其他人员，比如厨师和洗碗工。

words.meaning: n. 洗碗工（dishwasher 的复数）

sentences.en: To ensure that all employees were paid fair wages, some restaurants banned tipping and increased prices, but this movement toward no-tipping services has largely fizzled out.
sentences.cn: 为了确保所有员工都能拿到公平的工资，一些餐馆禁止给小费并提高了价格，但这种向无小费服务的转变在很大程度上已然失败了。

words.meaning: v. 禁止（ban 的过去式）
v. 以失败告终（fizzle 的过去分词，fizzle out 意为“失败”）

sentences.en: So, to increase employee wages without raising prices, more employers are succumbing to the temptations of tip creep and tipflation.
sentences.cn: 因此，为了在不提高价格的情况下增加员工工资，更多的雇主正屈服于小费渐涨和小费通胀的诱惑。

words.meaning: v. 屈服，抵挡不住（succumb 的现在分词）

sentences.en: However, many customers are frustrated because they feel they are being asked for too high of a tip, too often.
sentences.cn: 然而，许多顾客感到沮丧，因为他们觉得自己被索要过高的小费，且这种情况太过频繁。

sentences.en: And, as our research emphasizes, tipping now seems to be more coercive, less generous and often completely disassociated from service quality.
sentences.cn: 而且，正如我们的研究强调的那样，如今给小费似乎多了强制性、少了慷慨，而且往往与服务质量完全无关。

words.meaning: v. 强调（emphasize 的第三人称单数）

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 1, the practice of tipping in the U.S.
questions.stem_cn: 根据第一段可知，在美国给小费的做法

options.A: was regarded as a sign of generosity
options.C: was a way of rewarding diligence

options_cn.A: 被视为慷慨的一种标志
options_cn.B: 被认为对（餐馆）服务员来说极其重要
options_cn.C: 是奖励勤奋的一种方式
options_cn.D: 在多数企业中是可选择的

questions.explanation: 定位段[1]①句：美国顾客历来会给那些他们认为主要靠小费获取大部分收入的人小费，如低薪的餐馆服务员。由此可知，小费对餐馆服务员而言是重要收入来源、极其重要。B 项是对该句内容的合理推断，故正确。A、C 两项在段[1]中无法定位，属无中生有；D 项段[1]仅说明数字支付系统提醒顾客付小费，并未提及给小费可否选择，属无中生有。

questions.stem: Compared with tips in the past, today's tips
questions.stem_cn: 与过去的小费相比，如今的小费

options.B: are less often requested in advance
options.C: have less to do with service quality

options_cn.C: 与服务质量的关系不大
options_cn.D: 对工作者的收入贡献较小

questions.explanation: 综合段[2]①句与段[7]③句：过去的小费与服务标准（即服务质量）相关，而如今给小费往往与服务质量完全无关。C 项是对今昔小费差异的合理概括，故正确。A 项段[7]②句表明如今小费被索要得更频繁，反向干扰；B 项段[3]表明如今小费经常被提前索要，反向干扰；D 项段[5]表明如今小费对低薪工作者收入贡献更大，曲解文意。

questions.stem: Tip requests are creeping into new kinds of services as a result of
questions.stem_cn: 索要小费正逐渐出现在新型服务中是因为
questions.explanation: 定位段[4]①句：向顾客索要小费因数字支付设备的普及而变得更加容易，这正是索要小费出现在新型服务中的原因，而数字支付设备的普及属于科技进步的体现。A 项是对该原因的合理推断，故正确。B、D 属答非所问；C 项段[1]②句仅提及企业改用数字支付系统收款，并未提及业务多样化，属无中生有。

questions.stem: The movement toward no-tipping services was intended to
questions.stem_cn: 这种向无小费服务的转变的目的是
questions.explanation: 定位段[6]②句：一些餐馆禁止给小费并提高价格，是为了确保所有员工都能拿到公平的工资，即确保收入公平。D 项是对该转变目的的同义转述，故正确。A、C 均曲解文意（转变的做法是提高价格而非维持合理价格）；B 项段[5]表明向无小费服务转变会减少工作者的收入来源，反向干扰。

questions.stem: It can be learned from the last paragraph that tipping
questions.stem_cn: 从最后一段可以得知，给小费

options.A: is becoming a burden for customers
options.D: reflects the need to reduce prices

options_cn.A: 正成为顾客的一种负担
options_cn.D: 反映了降低价格的需求

questions.explanation: 结合段[7]②③句：如今给小费不再是自愿行为，顾客因被频繁索要过高的小费而感到沮丧，且给小费更具强制性。可推知给小费正成为顾客的经济与心理负担。A 项是对给小费所带来影响的合理推断，故正确。B 项与段[7]③句“往往与服务质量完全无关”矛盾，反向干扰；C 项无依据；D 项“不提高价格”不等于“降低价格”，曲解文意。

articles.title: Rather Than 'Fixing' the NHS, We Need to Radically Rethink Our Approach to Health
articles.topic: 与其“修复”NHS，不如彻底反思英国的医疗方式：NHS 模式已过时、供不应求，作者主张关注社会因素、重构以医院为中心的医疗体系
articles.source: 2025 年考研英语（二）Text 2 · 原文与答案依据真题及解析 PDF

sentences.en: When it was established, the National Health Service (NHS) was visionary: offering high-quality, timely care to meet the dominant needs of the population it served.
sentences.cn: 英国国家医疗服务体系（NHS）创立之初颇具远见：提供优质、及时的医疗护理，以满足所服务人群的主要需求。

words.meaning: v. 建立，创立（establish 的过去分词）

sentences.en: Nearly 75 years on, with the UK facing very different health challenges, it is clear that the model is out of date.
sentences.cn: 然而将近75年过去了，英国面临着截然不同的医疗挑战，这一模式明显已经过时。

sentences.en: From life expectancy to cancer and infant mortality rates, we are lagging behind many of our peers.
sentences.cn: 从预期寿命到癌症死亡率和婴儿死亡率，我们都落后于许多同类国家。

words.meaning: n. 预期，期望（life expectancy 意为“预期寿命”）
v. 落后（lag 的现在分词）

sentences.en: With more than 6.8 million on waitlists, healthcare is becoming increasingly inaccessible for those who cannot opt to pay for private treatment; and the cost of providing healthcare is increasingly squeezing out investment in other public services.
sentences.cn: 由于医疗等待者名单上的人数超过680万，对于那些无法选择支付私立医疗费用的人来说，医疗服务变得越来越难以获得；而且提供医疗服务的成本也越来越严重地挤压着其他公共服务方面的资金投入。

words.meaning: n. 等待名单（waitlist 的复数）
adj. 难以获得的，无法接近的
v. 挤压（squeeze 的现在分词）

sentences.en: As demand for healthcare continues to grow, pressures on the workforce—which is already near breaking point—will only become more acute.
sentences.cn: 随着对医疗服务的需求持续增长，本就濒临崩溃的医疗人员所承受的压力只会更大。

sentences.en: Many of the answers to the crisis in health and care are well rehearsed.
sentences.cn: 针对医疗和护理危机的诸多解决办法都已被反复探讨过。

words.meaning: v. 反复排练，反复讲述（rehearse 的过去分词）

sentences.en: We need to be much better at reducing and diverting demand on health services, rather than simply managing it.
sentences.cn: 我们需要在减少和转移医疗服务需求方面做得更好，而不仅仅是管理这种需求。

words.meaning: v. 转移，使转向（divert 的现在分词）
v. 管理，处理（manage 的现在分词）

sentences.en: Much more needs to be invested in communities and primary care to reduce our reliance on hospitals.
sentences.cn: 社区和基础医疗方面的投入需要加大，以减少我们对医院的依赖。

words.meaning: v. 投资（invest 的过去分词）

sentences.en: And capacity in social care needs to be greater, to support the growing number of people living with long-term conditions.
sentences.cn: 同时，社会关怀方面的能力也需要提高，以帮助越来越多患有长期疾病的人。

sentences.en: Yet despite two decades of strategies and a number of major health reforms, we have failed to make meaningful progress on any of these aims.
sentences.cn: 然而，尽管二十年间制定了诸多战略并进行了多项重大医疗改革，我们在上述任意目标上都未能取得实质性进展。

words.meaning: n. 几十年（decade 的复数）
n. 战略，策略（strategy 的复数）
adj. 有意义的，实质性的

sentences.en: That is why the Reform think tank is launching a new programme of work, called "Reimagining health" and supported by ten former health ministers.
sentences.cn: 正因如此，“改革”智库正在推出一项名为“Reimagining health”的新工作计划，该计划得到了十位卫生部前部长的支持。

words.meaning: v. 推出，发起（launch 的现在分词）
n. 部长，大臣（minister 的复数）

sentences.en: Together, we are calling for a much more open and honest conversation about the future of health in the UK, and an "urgent rethink" of the hospital-centric model we retain.
sentences.cn: 我们共同呼吁就英国医疗的未来展开更开放、更坦诚的对话，并对我们现存的以医院为中心的医疗模式进行“紧急反思”。

sentences.en: This must begin with the question of how we maximise the health of the nation, rather than "fix" the NHS.
sentences.cn: 这必须从“我们如何最大限度地提升国民健康水平”这一问题入手，而非仅仅“修复”NHS。

sentences.en: It is estimated, for example, that healthcare accounts for only about 20% of health outcomes.
sentences.cn: 例如，据估计，只有约20%的健康结果是由医疗服务带来的。

words.meaning: v. 估计（estimate 的过去分词）
n. 结果，成果（outcome 的复数）

sentences.en: Much more important are the places we live, work and socialise—yet there is no clear cross-government strategy for improving these social determinants of health.
sentences.cn: 对健康影响更大的是我们生活、工作和社交的场所，然而并没有明确的跨政府部门战略来改善这些影响健康的社会因素。

words.meaning: n. 决定因素（determinant 的复数）

sentences.en: Worse, when policies like the national obesity strategy are scrapped, taxpayers are left with the heavy price tag of treating the illnesses, like diabetes, that result.
sentences.cn: 更糟糕的是，当国家肥胖症防治战略之类的政策被废除时，纳税人就得为治疗由此引发的疾病（如糖尿病）承担高昂的费用。

words.meaning: n. 纳税人（taxpayer 的复数）

sentences.en: Reform wants to ask how power and resources should be distributed in our health system.
sentences.cn: “改革”智库希望探讨在我们的医疗体系中权力和资源应该如何分配。

words.meaning: v. 分配，分布（distribute 的过去分词）

sentences.en: What health functions should remain at the centre, and what should be given to local leaders, often responsible for services that create health, and with a much better understanding of the needs of their populations?
sentences.cn: 哪些医疗职能应当保留在中央，哪些应下放给地方领导？地方领导往往负责关乎民众健康的服务工作，并且他们对当地民众的需求有着更深入的了解。

words.meaning: n. 职能，功能（function 的复数）
n. 人口，民众（population 的复数）

questions.stem: According to the first two paragraphs, the NHS
questions.stem_cn: 根据前两段可知，NHS

options.C: can barely retain its current employees
options.D: is rivalled by private medical services

options_cn.D: 面临私立医疗服务的竞争

questions.explanation: 定位段[2]②③句：等待医疗救治的人数庞大、医疗服务愈发难以获得，需求持续增长而医疗人员承受巨大压力，即医疗服务供不应求。可知 NHS 的服务模式已难以满足人们的需求。B 项是对段[2]②③句的合理概括，故正确。A 项由“成本挤压投入”过度推理为“资金不足”；C 项由“医疗人员压力大”过度推理为“留不住员工”；D 项仅提及部分人无法选择私立医疗，属无中生有。

questions.stem: One answer to the crisis in health and care is to
questions.stem_cn: 针对医疗和护理危机的一个解决办法是

options.B: lighten the burden on social care

questions.explanation: 定位段[3]③句：社区和基础医疗方面的投入需要加大，以减少对医院的依赖。C 项是对该句 Much more needs to be invested in ... primary care 的同义转述，故正确。A 项无依据（原文是减少对医院的依赖）；B 项段[3]④句是要提高社会关怀能力而非减轻其负担，曲解文意；D 项由此可推知社区分担的压力可能增加而非减少，反向干扰。

questions.stem: "Reimagining health" is aimed to
questions.stem_cn: “Reimagining health”旨在
questions.explanation: 综合段[4]③句（呼吁对以医院为中心的医疗模式进行“紧急反思”）与段[6]①句（探讨权力和资源在医疗体系中的分配），可推知该计划旨在反思、重构医疗模式。C 项是对其目的的合理推断，故正确。A、B 均无依据；D 项段[4]①句仅提及以往医疗改革效果不佳，并无“暂停与重启”之说，属无中生有。

questions.stem: To maximise the nation's health, the author suggests
questions.stem_cn: 为了最大限度地提升国民健康水平，作者建议

options.B: paying due attention to social factors
options.D: enhancing the quality of health care

options_cn.C: 重新评估主要的健康结果

questions.explanation: 定位段[5]③句：对健康影响更大的是人们生活、工作和社交的场所，然而目前并没有明确的跨政府部门战略来改善这些社会因素。可知社会因素未得到充分关注，作者建议关注社会因素。B 项是对段[5]③句的合理推断，故正确。A、C、D 三项在原文中均无相应建议依据，属无中生有。

questions.stem: It can be inferred that local leaders should
questions.stem_cn: 从文中可以推断出，地方领导应该

options.B: develop a stronger sense of responsibility
options.C: play a bigger role in the health system

options_cn.C: 在医疗体系中发挥更大的作用
options_cn.D: 更好地了解人们的健康需求

questions.explanation: 定位段[6]②句：探讨中央与地方领导的医疗职能分配，并指出地方领导在负责公众健康服务方面具有优势（更了解当地民众需求）。可推知地方领导应发挥优势、承担更多医疗职能。C 项是对段[6]②句的合理推断，故正确。A、B 均无依据；D 项“更了解民众需求”是地方领导已具备的优势，并非未来应做之事，曲解文意。

articles.title: Heat-Proofing India: Cities in India Are Testing Measures That Could Help Urban Populations Worldwide Cope With Rising Temperatures
articles.topic: 印度城市试点应对高温行动计划（HAPs）：现有 HAPs 执行不均、预警阈值未本地化，应纳入湿度等多因素、绘制脆弱性地图，并追求让社区变凉爽的中长期目标
articles.source: 2025 年考研英语（二）Text 3 · 原文与答案依据真题及解析 PDF

sentences.en: Heat action plans, or HAPs, have been proliferating in India in the past few years.
sentences.cn: 在过去几年里，应对高温行动计划（HAPs）在印度迅速增多。

words.meaning: v. 激增，迅速增多（proliferate 的现在分词）

sentences.en: In general, an HAP spells out when and how officials should issue heat warnings and alert hospitals and other institutions.
sentences.cn: 通常，应对高温行动计划会详细说明官员发布高温预警并向医院及其他机构发出预警的时间及方式。

words.meaning: n. 警告，预警（warning 的复数）

sentences.en: Nagpur's plan, for instance, calls for hospitals to set aside "cold wards" in the summer for treating heatstroke patients, and advises builders to give construction laborers a break from work on very hot days.
sentences.cn: 例如，那格浦尔市的计划要求医院在夏季留出“清凉病房”来救治中暑患者，还建议建筑商让建筑工人在酷热天气停工休息。

words.meaning: n. 工人，劳动者（laborer 的复数）

sentences.en: But implementation of existing HAPs has been uneven, according to a report from the Center for Policy Research.
sentences.cn: 然而，政策研究中心的一份报告显示，现有的HAPs的执行情况参差不齐。

words.meaning: adj. 不均衡的，参差不齐的

sentences.en: Many lack adequate funding, it found.
sentences.cn: 该报告发现，许多HAPs都缺乏足够的资金支持。

sentences.en: And their triggering thresholds often are not customized to the local climate.
sentences.cn: 而且警报的触发阈值往往不是根据当地气候定制的。

words.meaning: v. 触发（trigger 的现在分词）
n. 阈值，门槛（threshold 的复数）
v. 定制（customize 的过去分词）

sentences.en: In some areas, high daytime temperatures alone might serve as an adequate trigger for alerts.
sentences.cn: 在某些地区，仅白天的高温就可能足以触发警报。

sentences.en: But in other places, nighttime temperatures or humidity might be as important a gauge of risk as daytime highs.
sentences.cn: 但在其他地方，夜间的温度或湿度可能与白天的最高气温一样，是衡量高温风险的重要指标。

sentences.en: Mumbai's April heatstroke deaths highlighted the need for more nuanced and localized warnings, researchers say.
sentences.cn: 研究人员表示，孟买4月份发生的中暑死亡事件凸显了更细致、更贴合当地情况的预警的必要性。

words.meaning: v. 凸显，强调（highlight 的过去式）

sentences.en: That day's high temperature of roughly 36°C was 1°C shy of the heat wave alert threshold for coastal cities set by national meteorological authorities.
sentences.cn: 那天的高温约为36℃，比国家气象部门为沿海城市设定的热浪警报阈值低1℃。

sentences.en: But the effects of the heat were amplified by humidity—an often neglected factor in heat alert systems—and the lack of shade at the late-morning outdoor ceremony.
sentences.cn: 但湿度（高温预警系统中经常被忽视的因素）以及上午晚些时候的户外仪式现场缺少阴凉处，使得高温的影响更加严重。

words.meaning: v. 放大，增强（amplify 的过去分词）
v. 忽视（neglect 的过去分词）

sentences.en: To help improve HAPs, urban planner Kotharkar's team is working on a model plan that outlines best practices and could be adapted to local conditions.
sentences.cn: 为了帮助改进HAPs，城市规划师Kotharkar的团队正在制定一个示范计划，该计划概述了最佳实践做法，且能够根据当地情况进行调整。

words.meaning: v. 概述（outline 的第三人称单数）
v. 调整，使适应（adapt 的过去分词）
n. 条件，情况（condition 的复数）

sentences.en: Among other things, she says, all cities should create a vulnerability map to help focus responses on the populations most at risk.
sentences.cn: 她说，除此之外，所有城市都应该绘制一份脆弱性地图，以帮助将应对措施重点聚焦在最有风险的人群上。

words.meaning: n. 人口，人群（population 的复数）

sentences.en: Such mapping doesn't need to be complex, Kotharkar says.
sentences.cn: Kotharkar表示，绘制这样的地图并不需要很复杂。

sentences.en: "A useful map can be created by looking at even a few key parameters."
sentences.cn: “即使只考虑几个关键因素，也能绘制出一张有用的地图。”

words.meaning: n. 参数，因素（parameter 的复数）

sentences.en: For example, neighborhoods with a large elderly population or informal dwellings that cope poorly with heat could get special warnings or be bolstered with cooling centers.
sentences.cn: 例如，可以给老年人口众多的街区或应对高温能力不足的非正式住宅区发送特别预警，或者在这些街区或非正式住宅区中设立降温中心以增强其应对能力。

words.meaning: n. 街区，社区（neighborhood 的复数）
adj. 年老的，上了年纪的
v. 增强，支持（bolster 的过去分词）

sentences.en: The Nagpur project has already created a risk and vulnerability map, which enabled Kotharkar to tell officials which neighborhoods to focus on in the event of a heat wave this summer.
sentences.cn: 那格浦尔市的计划已经绘制了一份风险和脆弱性地图，这使得Kotharkar能够告知官员们，如果今年夏天热浪来袭，应该关注哪些街区。

words.meaning: v. 使能够（enable 的过去式）

sentences.en: HAPs shouldn't just include short-term emergency responses, researchers say, but also recommend medium- to long-term measures that could make communities cooler.
sentences.cn: 研究人员称，HAPs不应只包含短期应急响应措施，还应提出能让社区变得更凉爽的中长期措施。

words.meaning: n. 紧急情况，突发事件

sentences.en: In Nagpur, for example, Kotharkar's team has been able to advise city officials about where to plant trees to provide shade.
sentences.cn: 例如，在那格浦尔市，Kotharkar的团队已经能够就在何处种树以提供阴凉处的问题向市政官员提出建议。

sentences.en: HAPs could also guide efforts to retrofit homes or modify building regulations.
sentences.cn: HAPs还可以指导房屋改造工作或建筑规范修订工作。

words.meaning: n. 规章，条例（regulation 的复数）

sentences.en: "Reducing deaths in an emergency is a good target to have, but it's the lowest target," says climate researcher Chandni Singh.
sentences.cn: 气候研究人员Chandni Singh表示：“减少在紧急情况下的死亡人数是一个不错的目标，但这只是最低目标。”

words.meaning: v. 减少（reduce 的现在分词）

articles.title: Phenomena: What Desire Paths Reveal About Human Nature
articles.topic: 心选小路（desire paths）揭示的人性：它们是人们追求便利的集体选择，反映公共空间由使用者主导的自然演变与追求可控城市环境之间的张力，并体现人与动物共有的特性
articles.source: 2025 年考研英语（二）Text 4 · 原文与答案依据真题及解析 PDF

sentences.en: Navigating beyond the organised pavements and parks of our urban spaces, desire paths are the unofficial footprints of a community, revealing the unspoken preferences, shared shortcuts and collective choices of humans.
sentences.cn: 在我们城市空间中规划好的人行道和公园之外，心选小路是社区的非正式足迹，它揭示了人们心照不宣的偏好、共享的捷径和集体的选择。

words.meaning: v. 通行，导航（navigate 的现在分词）
adj. 非官方的，非正式的
adj. 未说出口的，心照不宣的

sentences.en: Often appearing as trodden dirt tracks through otherwise neat green spaces, these routes of collective disobedience cut corners, bisect lawns and cross hills, representing the natural capability of people (and animals) to go from point A to point B most effectively.
sentences.cn: 这些集体不遵守规则而形成的路径常常以踩踏而成的土路形式出现在原本整洁的绿地中，它们抄近道、穿过草坪、越过山丘，体现了人类（以及动物）从A点到B点最高效移动的本能。

words.meaning: v. 踩，踏（tread 的过去分词）
v. 把……一分为二，二等分

sentences.en: Urban planners interpret desire paths as more than just convenient shortcuts; they offer valuable insights into the dynamics between planning and behaviour.
sentences.cn: 城市规划者认为，心选小路不仅仅是方便的捷径，它们还为规划与行为之间的动态关系提供了宝贵的见解。

sentences.en: Ohio State University allowed its students to navigate the Oval, a lawn in the centre of campus, freely, then proceeded to pave the desire paths, creating a web of effective routes students had established.
sentences.cn: 俄亥俄州立大学允许学生自由穿行校园中心的Oval草坪，继而铺砌这些学生走出的心选小路，创建出一个由学生开辟的有效路线网络。

words.meaning: v. 建立，开辟（establish 的过去分词）

sentences.en: Yet, reluctance persists among other planners to integrate desire paths into formal plans, citing concerns about safety, environmental impact, or primarily, aesthetics.
sentences.cn: 然而，其他规划者坚持不愿将心选小路纳入正式规划，他们担心安全问题、环境影响，或主要是美观问题。

sentences.en: A Reddit webpage devoted to the phenomenon, boasting nearly 50,000 members, showcases images of local desire paths adorned with signs instructing pedestrians to adhere to designated walkways, underscoring the rebellious nature inherent in these human-made tracks.
sentences.cn: 一个专门讨论这一现象且拥有近5万名成员的Reddit网页，展示了当地心选小路的图片，这些小路设有指示行人遵循指定走道的标志，这凸显了这些人为踏出的小路所固有的反叛属性。

words.meaning: v. 拥有（值得自豪的事物）（boast 的现在分词）
v. 装饰，装点（adorn 的过去分词）

sentences.en: This clash highlights an ongoing struggle between the organic, user-driven evolution of public spaces and the desire for a visually curated and controlled urban environment.
sentences.cn: 这一矛盾凸显了一种持续存在的斗争，它发生在公共空间由使用者主导的自然演变与追求看上去精心规划且可控的城市环境之间。

words.meaning: adj. 精心组织的，精心策划的

sentences.en: The Wickquasgeck Trail is an example of a historical desire path, created by Native Americans to cross the forests of Manhattan and move between settlements quickly.
sentences.cn: Wickquasgeck Trail是历史上心选小路的一个典型代表，它由美洲原住民开辟，用于穿越曼哈顿的森林并快速往返于各个定居点之间。

words.meaning: n. 定居点，聚居地（settlement 的复数）

sentences.en: This trail, when Dutch colonists arrived, was widened and made into one of the main trade roads across the island, known at the time as de Heere Straat, or Gentlemen's Street.
sentences.cn: 荷兰殖民者到来后，这条小路被拓宽，并成为岛上的主要贸易道路之一，当时被称为de Heere Straat，即Gentlemen's Street。

words.meaning: n. 殖民者（colonist 的复数）
v. 拓宽，加宽（widen 的过去分词）

sentences.en: Following the British assumption of control in New York, the street was renamed Broadway.
sentences.cn: 在英国人接管纽约后，这条街道被改名为百老汇。

words.meaning: v. 重新命名，改名（rename 的过去分词）

sentences.en: Notably, Broadway stands out as one of the few areas in NYC that defies the grid-based system applied to the rest of the city, cutting a diagonal across parts of the city.
sentences.cn: 值得注意的是，百老汇是纽约市少数几个打破该市其他地区采用的网格布局系统的区域之一，它斜穿部分城区。

words.meaning: v. 违抗，打破（defy 的第三人称单数）

sentences.en: In online spaces, desire paths have sparked a fascination that can approach obsession, with the Reddit page serving as a hub.
sentences.cn: 在网络世界中，心选小路激起了近乎痴迷的强烈兴趣，Reddit网页则成了这一现象的中心。

sentences.en: Contributors offer a wide array of stories, from little-known new shortcuts to long-established alternate routes.
sentences.cn: 投稿者们分享了形形色色的故事，从鲜为人知的新捷径到存在已久的替代路线。

words.meaning: n. 投稿者，贡献者（contributor 的复数）

sentences.en: Animal desire paths, such as ducks forging trails through frozen ponds or dogs carving direct routes in gardens, highlight the adaptability of these trails in both human and animal experiences.
sentences.cn: 动物的心选小路，如鸭子在池塘的冰面上开辟的小路，或狗在花园里开辟的直达路线，凸显了这些小路在人类和动物经历中的适应性。

words.meaning: v. 开辟，艰难前行（forge 的现在分词）
v. 开辟，雕刻（carve 的现在分词）

sentences.en: As desire paths criss-cross through both physical and virtual landscapes, they stand as a proof of the collective insistence on forging unconventional routes and embracing the spirit of communal choice.
sentences.cn: 随着心选小路在现实和虚拟景观中纵横交错，它们证明了人们集体坚持开辟非传统路线并拥抱集体选择的精神。

words.meaning: adj. 非传统的，非常规的

questions.explanation: 定位段[6]①句：动物也会为自己开辟心选小路，这凸显了心选小路在人类和动物经历中的适应性。可推知人类和动物在这方面存在共同的特性。D 项是对段[6]①句的合理推断，故正确。A、B 两项在段[6]中均无法定位，属无中生有；C 项曲解文意（心选小路是人与动物各自适应环境的结果，并非人类对动物行为的模仿）。

articles.title: Five Steps to Suggesting a Change at Work That'll Actually Get Taken Seriously
articles.topic: 新题型（小标题对应）：为文章各段落匹配恰当的小标题，介绍在工作中提出变革建议的五个步骤。

sentences.en: Everyone wants to be that person—the one who looks at the same information as everyone else, but who sees a fresh, innovative solution.
sentences.cn: 每个人都想成为那样的人——和其他人看到同样的信息，却能想出新颖的、创新的解决方案的人。

sentences.en: However, it takes more than simply having a good idea.
sentences.cn: 然而，仅仅有一个好想法是不够的。

sentences.en: How you share it is as important as the suggestion itself.
sentences.cn: 你分享建议的方式和建议本身一样重要。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.cn: 为什么呢？

sentences.en: Because writing a new script—literally or figuratively—means that other team members will have to adapt to something new.
sentences.cn: 因为无论是从字面意义还是从比喻意义上讲，编写一个新剧本（提出新的建议）意味着其他团队成员将不得不适应新事物。

sentences.en: So whether you're suggesting a (seemingly) benign change like streamlining outdated protocol, or a bigger change like adding an hour to each workday so people can leave early on Fridays, you're asking others to reimagine their workflow or schedule.
sentences.cn: 因此，无论你是提出一个（看似）无关痛痒的变革建议，比如简化过时的协议，还是提出一个更重大的变革建议，比如每天增加一小时工作时间以便人们周五能早点下班，你都是在要求他人重新设想他们的工作流程或日程安排。

sentences.en: Not to mention, if the process you're scrapping is one someone else suggested, there's the possibility of hurt feelings.
sentences.cn: 更不用说，如果你要摒弃的流程是别人提出的，那还可能会伤害他们的感情。

sentences.en: To gain buy-in on an innovative, new idea, follow these steps:
sentences.cn: 要想让一个创新的新想法获得认可，可遵循以下步骤：

sentences.en: Great ideas don't stand alone.
sentences.cn: 好的想法不会孤立存在。

sentences.en: In other words, you can't mention your suggestion once and expect it to be adopted.
sentences.cn: 换句话说，你不能只提一次你的建议就指望它被采纳。

sentences.en: To see a change, you'll need to champion your plan and sell its merits.
sentences.cn: 要想看到改变，你需要捍卫你的计划并推销它的优点。

sentences.en: In addition, you need to be willing to stand up to scrutiny and criticism and be prepared to explain your innovation in different ways for various audiences.
sentences.cn: 此外，你要愿意经受审查和批判，并愿意以不同的方式向不同的听众解释你的新想法。

sentences.en: Sometimes it makes sense to go to your boss first.
sentences.cn: 有时候先去找你的上司是明智之举。

sentences.en: But other times, it's useful to build a coalition among your co-workers or other stakeholders.
sentences.cn: 但其他时候，在你的同事或其他利益相关者中建立联盟是很有用的。

sentences.en: When it works, it works great—because you're ready for your stubborn supervisor's pushback with answers like, "Actually, I connected with a few people in our tech department to discuss how much time these kinds of website updates would take, and they suggested they have the bandwidth."
sentences.cn: 当这种方法奏效时，效果就会非常好——因为你已经准备好用这样的回答来应对固执的上司的反对：“实际上，我和我们技术部门的一些人已经交流过，讨论了这类网站更新需要花费多少时间，他们表示自己有精力来做这件事。”

sentences.en: One of the biggest barriers to gaining buy-in occurs when the owner of an idea is viewed as argumentative, defensive, or close-minded.
sentences.cn: 当某个想法的提出者被视为好争辩的、有戒心的或思想保守的人时，获得认可的最大障碍之一就出现了。

sentences.en: Because, let's be honest: No one likes a know-it-all.
sentences.cn: 因为，说实话：没人喜欢自以为无所不知的人。

sentences.en: So, if people disagree with you, don't be indignant.
sentences.cn: 所以，如果人们不同意你的观点，不要感到愤怒。

sentences.en: Instead, listen to their concerns fully, try to understand their perspective, and include their concerns (and possible remedies) in future discussions.
sentences.cn: 相反，要充分倾听他们的担忧，试着理解他们的观点，并将他们的担忧（以及可能的解决办法）纳入未来的讨论。

sentences.en: So, instead of saying, "Martha, our current slogan is confusing and should be updated," you could try, "Martha raises a great point that our current slogan has a long history for our stakeholders, but I wonder if we might be able to brainstorm a tagline that could build on that—and be clearer for new customers."
sentences.cn: 因此，不要说“玛莎，我们当前的标语很令人费解，应该更新一下”，你可以试着说“玛莎提出了一个很好的观点，我们当前的标语对我们的利益相关者来说有着悠久的历史，但我在想，我们能否集思广益，想出一个既能以此为基础又能让新客户更明白的标语”。

sentences.en: New ideas are the grandchildren of old ones.
sentences.cn: 新想法是旧想法的衍生物。

sentences.en: In other words, don't throw old solutions under the bus to make your improvement stand out.
sentences.cn: 换句话说，不要为了凸显你的改进而否定旧的解决方案。

sentences.en: Remember that in light of whatever the problem the old system solved—or, maybe, has failed to solve in recent memory—it was a great idea at the time.
sentences.cn: 记住，考虑到旧体系解决过的任何问题——或者，也许在最近未能解决什么问题——它在当时都是个很棒的想法。

sentences.en: Appreciating the older contributions as you suggest future innovations helps bolster the credibility of your idea.
sentences.cn: 在你提议未来的新想法时，赞赏过去的贡献有助于增强你的想法的可信度。

sentences.en: When pitching a new idea, it's important to use the language of abundance instead of the language of deficit.
sentences.cn: 在推销新想法时，使用富足性语言（积极的语言）而非匮乏性语言（消极的语言）至关重要。

sentences.en: Instead of saying what is wrong, broken, or suboptimal, talk about what is right, fixable, or ideal.
sentences.cn: 不要说什么是错的、有问题的或不太理想的，而要谈论什么是正确的、可解决的或理想的。

sentences.en: For example, try, "I can see lots of applications for this new approach" rather than, "This innovation is the only way."
sentences.cn: 例如，试着说“我能看到这种新方法有很多应用（场景）”，而不是说“这种创新是唯一的办法”。

sentences.en: Be optimistic but realistic, and you will stand out.
sentences.cn: 要保持乐观但也要实事求是，这样你就能脱颖而出。

questions.stem: 第 41 题：为第 2 段选择最合适的小标题
questions.explanation: 【推测段意】本段讲述了好的想法需要捍卫与推销以使其被接受，并提到推销过程中所面临的挑战。推测出的段意中的“好的想法需要推销”符合由F项预测的内容中的“介绍需要被推销的事物”。本段指出你需要推销自己的想法以使其被接受，并提到推销过程中可能面临的挑战，其中sell与F选项中的salesman相对应。故选F。

questions.stem: 第 42 题：为第 3 段选择最合适的小标题
questions.explanation: 【推测段意】本段讲述了提建议或想法时可以使用的两种渠道：找上司、在同事或其他利益相关者中建立联盟。推测出的段意中的“提建议或想法时可以使用的两种渠道”符合由C项预测的内容中的“介绍可以利用的渠道”。本段中的“找上司”和“在同事或其他利益相关者中建立联盟”为两种具体的可以利用的渠道。故选C。

questions.stem: 第 43 题：为第 4 段选择最合适的小标题
questions.explanation: 【推测段意】本段指出不谦逊的人所提出的想法可能不那么容易被认可，并说明在提出想法时需要保持谦逊以及如何保持谦逊。推测出的段意中的“在提出想法时需要保持谦逊以及如何保持谦逊”符合由G项预测的段意“保持谦逊的方法或重要性”。本段首句和②句指出不谦逊的后果，侧面说明保持谦逊的重要性；③④句说明了保持谦逊的做法。故选G。

questions.stem: 第 44 题：为第 5 段选择最合适的小标题
questions.explanation: 【推测段意】本段讲述了新想法与旧想法之间的关系以及提出新想法时尊重旧想法的重要性。本段尾句指出，在提议未来的新想法时，赞赏过去的贡献有助于增强你的想法的可信度，即尊重过去（Respect the past）的重要性。故选B。

questions.stem: 第 45 题：为第 6 段选择最合适的小标题
questions.explanation: 【推测段意】本段讲述了推销新想法时使用积极且切合实际的语言的重要性，并提供了具体的做法。推测出的段意符合由A项预测的段意“保持积极的方法或重要性”。本段首句指出推销新想法时使用积极的语言很重要，②句说明了使用积极的语言的具体做法，尾句再次点明保持积极态度的重要性，且尾句中的Be optimistic与A项Stay positive表意相同。故选A。

articles.title: Why You're Reluctant to Ask for Help... and How to Get Over It
articles.topic: 完形填空：你为什么难以开口寻求帮助——分析人们不愿求助的原因（担心暴露弱点、被人拒绝等），并给出克服困难、勇敢求助的方法。

sentences.en: There are many understandable reasons why you might find it difficult to ask for help when you need it.
sentences.cn: 有许多合情合理的原因可以解释为什么当你需要帮助时你可能会觉得开口求助很难。

sentences.en: Psychologists have been interested in this [1] question for decades, not least because people's widespread [2] reluctance to ask for help has led to some high-profile failures.
sentences.cn: 几十年来，心理学家一直对这个问题感兴趣，尤其是因为人们普遍不愿寻求帮助已经导致了一些广受关注的失败事件。

sentences.en: Asking for help takes [3] courage.
sentences.cn: 寻求帮助需要勇气。

sentences.en: It involves communicating a need on your part—there's something you can't do.
sentences.cn: 它需要你表达自己的需求，即有些事情你做不到。

sentences.en: [4] In other words, you're broadcasting your own weaknesses, which can be [5] uncomfortable.
sentences.cn: 换句话说，你在公开自己的弱点，这可能是令人担忧的。

sentences.en: You might worry about coming across as incompetent.
sentences.cn: 你可能担心给人留下无能的印象。

sentences.en: You might have [6] concerns about losing control of whatever it is you're asking for help with.
sentences.cn: 你可能会担心对你正在寻求帮助的事情失去控制权。

sentences.en: [7] Once someone starts to help, perhaps they'll take over, or get credit for your earlier efforts.
sentences.cn: 一旦有人开始帮助你，也许他们会接手（你所求助的事情），或者将你之前的努力都归功于自己。

sentences.en: Yet another [8] factor that you might be worried about is being a nuisance or [9] inconveniencing the person you go to for help.
sentences.cn: 又一个你可能担心的因素是，你会惹人厌烦或给你前去求助的人带来不便。

sentences.en: If you struggle with low self-esteem, you might find it especially difficult to [10] reach out for help because you have the added worry of the other person [11] declining your request.
sentences.cn: 如果你受自卑感困扰，你可能会觉得向他人寻求帮助尤其困难，因为你还担心对方拒绝你的请求。

sentences.en: You might see such refusals as implying something [12] negative about the status of your relationship with them.
sentences.cn: 你可能会把这种拒绝看作你们关系状态的某种负面暗示。

sentences.en: To [13] overcome these difficulties, try to remind yourself that everyone needs help sometimes.
sentences.cn: 为了克服这些困难，试着提醒自己，每个人都有需要帮助的时候。

sentences.en: Nobody knows everything and can do everything all by themselves.
sentences.cn: 没有人无所不知，也没人能独自完成所有的事情。

sentences.en: And while you might [14] fear coming across as incompetent, there's actually research that shows that advice-seekers are [15] perceived as more competent, not less.
sentences.cn: 而且，尽管你可能担心给人留下无能的印象，但实际上有研究表明，寻求建议的人被认为更有能力，而非能力较差。

sentences.en: Perhaps most encouraging of all is a paper from 2022 by researchers at Stanford University, in California, that involved a mix of contrived help-seeking interactions and asking people to [16] recall times they'd sought help in the past.
sentences.cn: 或许最令人鼓舞的是加利福尼亚州斯坦福大学的研究人员在2022年发布的一份研究报告，该报告包含了人为设计的求助互动情景并让参与者回忆他们过去寻求帮助的（真实）经历。

sentences.en: The findings showed that help-seekers generally underestimate how [17] willing other people will be to help and how good it'll make the help-giver feel [for most people, having the chance to help someone is highly [18] rewarding].
sentences.cn: 研究结果表明，求助者通常会低估他人多么愿意帮忙以及帮助别人让施助者多么愉悦【对大多数人来说，有机会帮助别人是非常有意义的】。

sentences.en: So, bear all this in mind the next time you need to ask for help.
sentences.cn: 所以，下次你需要寻求帮助时，请记住这一切。

sentences.en: [19] Also, take care over who you ask and when you ask them.
sentences.cn: 此外，要谨慎选择求助对象及求助时机。

sentences.en: And if someone can't help right now, avoid taking it personally.
sentences.cn: 如果有人当下无法提供帮助，不要往心里去。

sentences.en: They might just be too [20] busy, or they might not feel confident about their ability to help.
sentences.cn: 他们可能只是太忙了，或者对自己提供帮助的能力没有信心。

questions.stem: 第 1 空：选择最合适的词填入空白 [1]

questions.explanation: 词义辨析。结合第1、2题选项分析空格所在句（段[1]②句）的语法结构可知：段[1]②句结构是“主句+原因状从”，空格位于主句中，与in this共同构成介词短语，作状语。【看本句】本句提到，心理学家一直对“这个事物”感兴趣。【看上文】本段①句提到，有许多合情合理的原因可以解释为什么当你需要帮助时你可能会觉得开口求助很难。【提要点】“这个事物”指代①句中提到的“为什么当你需要帮助时你可能会觉得开口求助很难”这一问题，由此可知，心理学家一直对这个问题感兴趣。综上可知，空格所填词应表示“问题”。D项question符合要求，故正确。

questions.explanation: 词义辨析。结合第1题的分析可知：段[1]②句结构是“主句+原因状从”，空格位于原因状语从句中，与people's widespread共同构成名词短语作主语。【看本句】本句提到，心理学家一直对这个问题感兴趣，尤其是因为人们普遍存在的对于寻求帮助的情感态度或行为趋势已经导致了一些广受关注的失败事件。“需要帮助时觉得开口求助很难”表明人们不愿开口求助的态度和倾向。综上可知，人们普遍不情愿寻求帮助。A项reluctance符合要求，故正确。

questions.stem: 第 3 空：选择最合适的词填入空白 [3]
questions.explanation: 词义辨析。结合选项分析空格所在句（段[2]①句）的语法结构可知：段[2]①句的主干结构是“主+谓+宾”，空格处在句中作宾语。【看本句】本句提到，寻求帮助需要____。【看下文】段[2]②句提到，它（寻求帮助）需要你表达自己的需求，即有些事情你做不到。【提要点】寻求帮助需要表明自己无法做到某些事，即正视并承认自己的不足。而正视并承认自己的不足需要个体具备勇敢的品质和豁达的心态。综上可知，空格处应表示与“勇敢”“豁达”相关的含义。C项courage可表示“勇气；胆量”，符合要求，故正确。

questions.stem: 第 4 空：选择最合适的词填入空白 [4]
questions.explanation: 逻辑关系。结合第4、5题选项分析空格所在句（段[2]③句）的语法结构可知：段[2]③句结构是“主句+定从”，空格位于句首，在句中作插入语。【看本句】本句提到，你在公开自己的弱点。【看上文】段[2]②句提到，它（寻求帮助）需要你表明自己无法做到某些事情。【提要点】空格所在句提到的“你在公开自己的弱点”是对②句提到的“你要表明自己无法做到某些事情”的解释说明。综上可知，空格处应能体现本句与段[2]②句之间解释说明的逻辑关系。B项In other words符合要求，故正确。

questions.stem: 第 5 空：选择最合适的词填入空白 [5]

options_cn.D: 令人担忧的，令人不安的

questions.explanation: 词义辨析。结合第4题的分析可知：段[2]③句结构是“主句+定从”，空格位于从句中作表语，应体现主语which（指代“你在公开自己的弱点”）的某种特点。【看本句】本句提到，你在公开自己的弱点，这可能是____。【看下文】段[2]④句提到，你可能担心给人留下无能的印象。【提要点】段[2]④句是对③句的进一步说明，指出了公开自己的弱点可能会让自己担心给人留下无能的印象。综上可知，公开自己的弱点可能是令人担忧的。D项uncomfortable符合要求，故正确。

questions.explanation: 词义辨析。结合选项分析空格所在句（段[2]⑤句）的语法结构可知：段[2]⑤句的主干结构是“主+谓+宾”，空格处在本句中作宾语，被介词短语about losing control of...help with修饰。【看上文】段[2]③句提到，公开自己的弱点（即向他人求助）可能会令自己感到担忧，接着④句指出一种具体的担忧：担心给人留下无能的印象。【提要点】与④句相似，⑤句中的“对正在寻求帮助的事情失去控制权”也是一种在求助时会给人带来不安感的具体担忧。综上可知，空格处应表示“担心；担忧”。B项concerns符合要求，故正确。

questions.stem: 第 7 空：选择最合适的词填入空白 [7]

articles.title: Why Do We Panic in Silences During Conversations?
articles.topic: 翻译：交谈中的沉默——介绍研究者对谈话中停顿的分析，说明陌生人之间的长停顿与朋友之间的长停顿会带来截然不同的影响。
articles.ref_cn: 你知道那种时刻吧——谈话慢了下来，然后出现了停顿。这种场面令人尴尬，尴尬到让一些人惊慌失措，只能随便说些什么。我们都认为这样的沉默让人倍感压力吗？研究者们分析了谈话期间超过2秒的停顿的发生率及影响，并回顾了先前一些研究的综述，这些研究表明，人们太过担心尴尬的沉默，以至于他们会避免和陌生人交谈，尽管这样做很可能会是一种令人愉快的体验。在有短暂停顿的谈话中，人们感觉与其交谈对象的关系更加亲密。然而，当谈话陷入长时间的停顿时，这种亲密感会显著降低。陌生人之间谈话的长时间停顿易于引发话题的转换。但是，对于朋友之间的谈话，情况似乎恰好相反。在这种情况下，长时间的停顿使彼此的关系更加亲密。朋友之间，较长时间的停顿似乎给仔细思考和表情流露提供了自然而然的时机。

sentences.en: You know the moment—the conversation slows, then there's a pause.
sentences.cn: 你知道那种时刻吧——谈话慢了下来，然后出现了停顿。

sentences.en: It's awkward, and so awkward that some people will panic and say anything.
sentences.cn: 这种场面令人尴尬，尴尬到让一些人惊慌失措，只能随便说些什么。

sentences.en: Do we all find such silences so stressful?
sentences.cn: 我们都认为这样的沉默让人倍感压力吗？

sentences.en: Researchers analysed the frequency and impact of gaps greater than 2 seconds during conversations, including an overview of previous studies which indicate that the fear of awkward silences can be so extreme that people avoid talking to strangers, even though doing so is likely to be an enjoyable experience.
sentences.cn: 研究者们分析了谈话期间超过2秒的停顿的发生率及影响，并回顾了先前一些研究的综述，这些研究表明，人们太过担心尴尬的沉默，以至于他们会避免和陌生人交谈，尽管这样做很可能会是一种令人愉快的体验。

sentences.en: During conversations with short gaps, people feel more connected to their conversation partners.
sentences.cn: 在有短暂停顿的谈话中，人们感觉与其交谈对象的关系更加亲密。

sentences.en: But such feelings of connection markedly dip when entering a long gap.
sentences.cn: 然而，当谈话陷入长时间的停顿时，这种亲密感会显著降低。

sentences.en: Long gaps between strangers are likely to be followed by a change in topic.
sentences.cn: 陌生人之间谈话的长时间停顿易于引发话题的转换。

sentences.en: But the opposite seems to be true for conversations between friends.
sentences.cn: 但是，对于朋友之间的谈话，情况似乎恰好相反。

sentences.en: Long gaps there saw increased connection.
sentences.cn: 在这种情况下，长时间的停顿使彼此的关系更加亲密。

sentences.en: Between friends, longer gaps seem to provide natural moments for reflection and expression.
sentences.cn: 朋友之间，较长时间的停顿似乎给仔细思考和表情流露提供了自然而然的时机。

articles.title: Part A 应用文：邀请信——邀请 John 参演改编自《三国演义》的短剧

articles.sample_en:
Dear John,

I'm currently planning a short play. I'm writing to invite you to act in the play.

The play is adapted from The Romance of the Three Kingdoms, which will start filming on December 30th. It will show the great stories of strategy, loyalty and heroism from this classic Chinese novel. articles.title: Part B 大作文：某社区老年人主要日常休闲活动调查（柱形图）
articles.topic: 大作文：根据柱形图写一篇约150词的短文，描述某社区老年人主要日常休闲活动的占比情况（90.8%/68.3%/34.7%/31.8%/18.4%）并发表评论。
articles.sample_en:
The given bar chart depicts the detailed information of the primary leisure activities of the elderly in a certain community. Those who choose to watch television make up the largest proportion of the respondents, up to 90.8%, and those who choose to take walks come second, at 68.3%. In contrast, those who favor planting flowers, reading and playing chess occupy smaller shares: 34.7%, 31.8% and 18.4% respectively.

The causes of these differences can be summarized as follows. First of all, watching television is an extremely convenient way to access information and enjoy entertainment, which is why the vast majority of elderly people choose it. Secondly, walking is a low-intensity outdoor activity suitable for many of the elderly. Besides, although planting flowers, reading and playing chess are also beneficial, more often than not, only the elderly who are interested in these activities will participate in them.

In short, diverse leisure activities play a crucial role in enriching the lifestyles of the elderly. Therefore, the elderly are advised to try more forms of leisure activities, besides the current ones, to bring more color to their lives.
articles.sample_cn:
题目所给的柱形图描述了某社区老年人的主要休闲活动的详细信息。选择看电视的人在受访者中所占的比例最大，达到90.8%，选择散步的人位居第二，占比68.3%。相比之下，喜欢养花、阅读和下棋的人占比较小：分别为34.7%、31.8%和18.4%。

引起这些差异的原因可以总结如下。首先，看电视是一种极为便捷的获取信息和享受娱乐的方式，这就是绝大多数老年人选择它的原因。其次，散步是一种低强度的户外活动，适合许多老年人。此外，尽管养花、阅读和下棋也是有益的活动，但往往只有对这些活动感兴趣的老年人才会参与其中。

总之，多样化的休闲活动在丰富老年人的生活方式中发挥着至关重要的作用。因此，除了当前这些休闲活动，建议老年人尝试更多类型的休闲活动，为他们的生活增添更多色彩。
